samples: Yes, I quite like it. It is mostly residential, so evenings are quiet, but there is a small high street within a ten-minute walk, which is convenient for groceries.
There is a park, a clinic, and two bus stops nearby. The nearest supermarket is a short walk away, and a community centre runs weekend classes for residents.
It has become a bit denser. A few apartment blocks replaced older houses, and more cafés opened, though the main park is still the same.
I prefer something in between. I want shops and transport nearby, but I do not want constant traffic noise outside my window at night.
I try to read a few evenings each week, usually for twenty or thirty minutes before bed. On busy weeks I manage less, but I still keep a book on my desk.
I prefer paper for novels because it is easier on my eyes, but I use an e-reader when I travel so I can carry several titles without extra weight.
As a child I liked adventure stories and simple science books with diagrams. I reread a few favourites many times instead of always buying new ones.
People may read fewer long books, but they still read a lot on screens. The form has changed more than the total amount of reading, in my view.

sampleNotes: Who: older woman at the station
Where/when: last winter, missed last bus
Help: called a taxi and waited with me
Feeling: relieved, wanted to repay kindness
sample-sp2-helpful-stranger.sampleAnswer: I want to talk about a winter evening last year when I missed the last bus home. I was standing at the bus stop with a heavy bag, checking the timetable again and again, when an older woman who had also been waiting noticed I looked upset. She asked what was wrong, and when I explained, she used her phone to call a taxi company and stayed with me until the car arrived so I would not wait alone in the dark. She even refused money for the call and just said she hoped someone would do the same for her grandchildren one day. Afterwards I felt relieved and a little embarrassed that I had needed help, but mostly grateful. The short conversation reminded me that small acts of kindness from strangers can change a stressful moment completely, and I try to notice when other people might need the same kind of support.
part3Samples: Some people worry about safety or feel unsure whether help is welcome. Others are simply busy and do not want to get involved in a situation they do not understand.
Yes, within reason. Organised volunteering can strengthen trust and give people practical ways to contribute, but it should not replace basic public services that everyone relies on.
Apps and messaging make it easier to request help quickly, from ride-hailing to neighbourhood groups. The downside is that face-to-face offers of help may feel less natural than before.
Not always. Small towns can feel closer, but large cities also have strong local networks. Kindness depends more on culture and individual habits than on city size alone.
